title: Contractibility of representable mapping sets into a polynomial-pair resolution
statement:
Let $A\to B$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings, let $E$ be a set, and put $C=B[E]$. Work in a common infinite size bound containing all rings and generator sets [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $\mathcal A$ be the category of compatible augmented polynomial pairs $(P\to B,Q\to C)$, where $P$ is polynomial over $A$ and $Q$ is polynomial over $P$, with commuting augmentation-preserving algebra-map pairs as morphisms; let $\mathcal B$ be the category of augmented polynomial $B$-algebras $T\to C$, and $v^+:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ the base-change functor $Q\otimes_P B$ [def-trf-polynomial-presentation-pair-categories]. Let $P_\bullet\to\operatorname{const} B$ be an augmented simplicial $A$-algebra, each $P_n$ polynomial over $A$ with generators in the bound [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-object]. Assume both $P_\bullet\to\operatorname{const} B$ and $P_\bullet[E]\to\operatorname{const} C$ are trivial Kan fibrations of underlying simplicial sets [def-weil-pbc-trivial-kan-fibration]. Then $U_n=(P_n\to B,P_n[E]\to C)$ with operators fixing $E$ defines a simplicial object of $\mathcal A$, transported through isomorphisms to the chosen small representatives if necessary. There is a canonical simplicial isomorphism $v^+U_\bullet\cong\operatorname{const}(C\xrightarrow{1}C)$, induced by $P_n[E]\otimes_{P_n}B\cong B[E]$ and fixing coefficients and variables. For every $W=(A[S]\xrightarrow{\beta}B,A[S][T]\xrightarrow{\gamma}C)$ in $\mathcal A$, there is an isomorphism of simplicial sets
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal A}(W,U_\bullet)\cong\prod_{s\in S}(P_\bullet\times_{\operatorname{const}B}\{\beta(X_s)\})\times\prod_{t\in T}(P_\bullet[E]\times_{\operatorname{const}C}\{\gamma(X_t)\}).$$
The unique map $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal A}(W,U_\bullet)\to *$ is a trivial Kan fibration and a homotopy equivalence to a singleton, for arbitrary, possibly empty or infinite, $S,T,E$.

source.place: Tag 08QV (lemma-polynomial-on-top), construction of U and product of representable fibres; simplicial.tex Tag 08NS (lemma-trivial-kan-homotopy).

proof.text: Write $\epsilon_n:P_n\to B$ for the augmentation. For every simplicial operator $u:P_n\to P_m$, extend $u$ to $u[E]:P_n[E]\to P_m[E]$ by applying $u$ to coefficients and fixing every $X_e$. The polynomial universal property [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring] implies $(u\circ w)[E]=u[E]\circ w[E]$ and $1[E]=1$. Since $\epsilon_m u=\epsilon_n$, the pairs $(u,u[E])$ preserve both augmentations. Thus the pairs $U_n$ and these operators form a simplicial object of the category in [def-trf-polynomial-presentation-pair-categories], with variance as in [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-object].

source.place: Tag 08QV (lemma-polynomial-on-top), first paragraph, construction of U; expressed in the ordinary algebra-map category, opposite to the source site.

proof.text: Each $P_n$ admits a polynomial presentation $A[S_n]\cong P_n$ with $S_n$ in the fixed bound. Choose these presentations once, and extend them fixing $E$ to isomorphisms of augmented pairs $i_n:\widetilde U_n\xrightarrow{\sim}U_n$. The small representative operator is $i_m^{-1}(u,u[E])i_n$. Composition cancels the middle $i_m i_m^{-1}$, so identities and all simplicial relations persist; postcomposition by $i_n$ identifies the two representable Hom sets in every degree and commutes with these operators. This realizes the replacement within [def-weil-size-convention] and [def-trf-polynomial-presentation-pair-categories].

source.place: Tag 08QV (lemma-polynomial-on-top), construction of U; explicit conjugation into the chosen bounded polynomial representatives.

proof.text: In the coordinate definition of $v^+$ in [def-trf-polynomial-presentation-pair-categories], the pair $(A[S_n]\to B,A[S_n][E]\to C)$ is sent to $(E,e\mapsto X_e)$, namely $C\xrightarrow{1}C$. Every induced operator is a $B$-algebra map fixing each $X_e$, hence is the identity by [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. Consequently these identifications give the claimed simplicial isomorphism $v^+U_\bullet\cong\operatorname{const}(C\xrightarrow{1}C)$. By the defining base-change identification of the cited category, its degree-$n$ map is $P_n[E]\otimes_{P_n}B\cong B[E]$ with $p\otimes b\mapsto\epsilon_n(p)b$ for coefficients $p\in P_n$, and $X_e\otimes1\mapsto X_e$.

source.place: Tag 08QV (lemma-polynomial-on-top), first paragraph: u_3(U) is constant; coordinate base-change functor from the construction before Tag 08QU.

proof.text: For $W=(A[S]\xrightarrow{\beta}B,A[S][T]\xrightarrow{\gamma}C)$, send a morphism $(f,g):W\to U_n$ to $(f(X_s))_{s\in S},(g(X_t))_{t\in T}$. Conversely, for elements $a_s\in P_n$ and $b_t\in P_n[E]$ with $\epsilon_n(a_s)=\beta(X_s)$ and $\epsilon_n[E](b_t)=\gamma(X_t)$, the polynomial universal property first gives the unique $A$-algebra map $f$ with $X_s\mapsto a_s$, and then the unique map $g$ whose restriction to $A[S]$ is $A[S]\xrightarrow f P_n\to P_n[E]$ and with $X_t\mapsto b_t$. The augmentations agree on coefficients and all generators, hence everywhere. These operations are inverse. Postcomposition by $(u,u[E])$ applies $u$ to each $a_s$ and $u[E]$ to each $b_t$, exactly the fibre-product operators. The bijections therefore give the displayed simplicial isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 08QV (lemma-polynomial-on-top), representable mapping set and its product of generator fibres; universal-property expansion.

proof.text: Let $p:X\to\operatorname{const}D$ be either assumed trivial Kan fibration and $d\in D$. For a boundary map into $F_d=X\times_{\operatorname{const}D}\{d\}$, compose with $F_d\to X$ and use the constant map $\Delta[n]\to\operatorname{const}D$ of value $d$. The lifting condition in [def-weil-pbc-trivial-kan-fibration] gives a simplex over $d$ extending the prescribed boundary, which therefore lies in $F_d$. In degree zero choose a preimage of $d$ using the required surjectivity of $p_0$. Hence $F_d\to *$ is a trivial Kan fibration. Apply this separately to every $\beta(X_s)\in B$ and $\gamma(X_t)\in C$.

source.place: Tag 08QV (lemma-polynomial-on-top), fibres F_s and F_t; simplicial.tex Tag 08NN (lemma-trivial-kan-base-change), here proved directly for fibres.

proof.text: A boundary map into the product of Step 4 projects to one boundary map in each factor. Step 5 supplies a filler in each factor; choose one for every index in the set $S\amalg T$ and take their tuple. Its restriction is the original boundary because this holds on each coordinate. The same coordinatewise choice gives a vertex of the product. This verifies both conditions in [def-weil-pbc-trivial-kan-fibration] for the product map to $*$. If $S\amalg T$ is empty, the product is already $*$ and the filler is the unique tuple. Transporting across Step 4 proves that $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal A}(W,U_\bullet)\to *$ is a trivial Kan fibration, without a finiteness hypothesis.

source.place: Tag 08QV (lemma-polynomial-on-top), product of generator fibres; simplicial.tex Tag 08NR (lemma-product-trivial-kan), coordinatewise lifting argument written out.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-trivial-kan-homotopy-equivalence] to the map $p:\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal A}(W,U_\bullet)\to *$ proved to be a trivial Kan fibration in Step 6. Its statement supplies a section $g$ with $p\circ g=1_*$ and a simplicial homotopy from the identity to $g\circ p$. These are precisely a homotopy inverse and the required homotopy equivalence to a singleton.

source.place: Tag 08NS (lemma-trivial-kan-homotopy), applied to the representable map to a singleton.

proof_origin.place: Tag 08QV (lemma-polynomial-on-top), construction and product-of-fibres argument, with simplicial.tex Tags 08NN, 08NR, 08NS; elementary universal-property and lifting details expanded.

Steps 1-4 check by the polynomial universal property and the pair-category definition: the operators fix E and preserve both augmentations; transport by conjugating with presentations extended fixing E; v+ of the transported U_n is literally (E, e->X_e) and its operators are the identity by uniqueness; Hom(W,U_n) is in bijection with generator tuples, and augmentation agreement on A[S] uses the compatibility of W's augmentations. Steps 5-6 are the fibre (08NN) and arbitrary-product (08NR) lifting arguments written out from the definition, with n=0 handled by surjectivity and the empty product equal to *; I accept them as elementary. Step 7 applies the 08NS node with Y=*. This departs from Stacks' products-of-homotopy-equivalences argument but is valid and simpler. Stacks derives that P[E]->C is trivial Kan by a filtered colimit; here it is a hypothesis, which the parent's Step 1 supplies.
